summary: splitlines separates text at recognized line boundaries and, by default, removes the boundary characters.
documentation: splitlines separates text at recognized line boundaries and, by default, removes the boundary characters. It understands LF, CR and CRLF, among other Unicode boundaries. A final line break does not add an extra trailing empty item.
returns: A list of lines without their line-ending characters.
caution: Internal blank lines remain empty strings. Empty text returns [], unlike splitting an empty string on a literal newline. This is not whitespace-token splitting.
scenarios: Read pasted notes with mixed operating-system line endings.
Preview imported line-oriented identifiers without trailing terminators.
Preserve blank lines when displaying a local multiline message.
title: Split mixed line endings
problem: Return input.splitlines() with line endings removed. Preserve internal blank lines, but do not add an extra empty line solely because the text ends in a line break.
hint: Use splitlines rather than split("\n") or split().
goal: Use str.splitlines() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
